translationRepairs: Yuan Faseng; Yuan Shu; Yuan Yuanda; Wang Shenian; Yang Hua; Yang Kan; Kun; Yang Yaren
Yuan Faseng; Yuan Shu; Yuan Yuanda; Wang Shenian; Yang Hua; Yang Kan; his son Kun; Yang Yaren
Idiomatic drops the kinship marker 子 present in the Chinese and literal, leaving bare Kun inconsistent with the other full names. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
Four years later he rose to Grand Commandant, bearing the golden seal of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
In the fourth year he advanced to Grand Commandant and concurrently held the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Ornament.

Chinese 四年 is the fourth year of Zhongdatong continued from the prior sentence, not an elapsed span of four years after the previous appointment. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.

In the fourth year he became General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Xuzhou and was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng, but did not take up the post; soon after he was relieved as Palace Attendant and Minister of Revenue.

In the fourth year he became General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Xuzhou and was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng, but did not take up the post; soon after he was appointed Palace Attendant and Minister of Revenue.
除 means to appoint to an office; rendering it as “relieved” reverses the sense. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
Hou Jing’s revolt led him to court Yuan Jingzhong as a puppet emperor, sending envoys with that pledge.
When Hou Jing rebelled, he sent word to entice Jingzhong, a member of the Yuan imperial clan, promising to install him as ruler.

Idiomatic “led him to court Yuan Jingzhong” garbles 遣信誘之 and obscures that Hou Jing was the sender enticing Jingzhong. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
His brother Jinglong had already served as Guangzhou inspector.
His elder brother Jinglong later became Inspector of Guangzhou.
Chinese 後爲 means ‘later became’; idiomatic ‘had already served’ reverses the temporal relation, and 兄 is specifically elder brother. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
He entered Wei service as a prefectural aide, became Yingchuan inspector, then surrendered the commandery to Liang.
He entered Wei service as a provincial registrar, became Grand Administrator of Yingchuan, then held the commandery and tendered his allegiance to Liang.
太守 is Grand Administrator (prefect), not regional inspector (刺史); the idiomatic English misrenders the office. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
He began his career in Wei as a commandery secretariat aide, rose to Inspector of Yingchuan, and then held the commandery and submitted in allegiance.
He began his career in Wei as a provincial registrar, gradually rose to Grand Administrator of Yingchuan, and then held the commandery and tendered his allegiance.
太守 is Grand Administrator, not Inspector; the literal English uses the wrong office title. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
Dugu Ruyuan relieved the city, then trapped Shu until it fell. Captured in Wei, he died of humiliation at forty-eight.
Dugu Ruyuan came to relieve the city and then besieged Shu. When the city fell, Shu was captured; he died in Wei of pent-up indignation at forty-eight.
發憤卒 means he died of grief or indignation, not humiliation. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
Zhongdatong year 2 brought him back as Palace Attendant, Grand Master for All, and General Who Assists the Left.
Zhongdatong year 2 brought him back as Palace Attendant, Grand Master of the Palace, and General Who Assists the Left.
太中大夫 is a court counselor title, not ‘Grand Master for All’. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
In the second year of Zhongdatong he was summoned as Palace Attendant, Grand Master for All, and General Who Assists the Left.
In the second year of Zhongdatong he was summoned as Palace Attendant, Grand Master of the Palace, and General Who Assists the Left.
太中大夫 should not be rendered ‘Grand Master for All’. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
His grandfather Gui served Song’s Emperor Wu when the latter was provisional Xuzhou inspector, joining his staff as libationer and Attendant for All.
His grandfather Gui was recruited as Libationer-Attendant and Grand Rectifier when the future Emperor Wu of Song governed Xuzhou.
大中正 is the Senior Rectifier, not “Attendant for All”; 祭酒從事 is Libationer-Attendant on the staff. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
His grandfather Gui, when Emperor Wu of Song was provisional inspector of Xuzhou, was summoned as Libationer and Attendant for All in the staff.
His grandfather Gui, when the future Emperor Wu of Song governed Xuzhou, was recruited as Libationer-Attendant and Grand Rectifier.
Same mistranslation of 大中正; render as Senior Rectifier and keep 祭酒從事 as Libationer-Attendant. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
His father had long dreamed of the south and told his sons, “No one should die a stranger—go back and serve the Liang.”
His father had long wished to return south and often told his sons, “How can a man remain long in a foreign land? You should return and serve the Eastern Court.”
東朝 is the Eastern Court; the idiomatic line invents “the Liang,” which is not in the Chinese. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
Year 8 made him Minister of the Court for Dependencies.
Year 8 made him Minister of Justice.
都官尚書 is the Minister of Justice / Capital Officials board, not a court for dependencies. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
In the eighth year he was transferred to Minister of the Court for Dependencies.
In the eighth year he was transferred to Minister of Justice.
都官尚書 denotes the justice/capital-officials ministry; Dependencies mistranslates the office. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
He never went forward; contemporaries praised his uprightness.
In the end, Kan would not receive him; contemporaries praised his uprightness.
竟不前之 means Kan would not let Zhang advance/sit; subject is refusal to admit, not Kan going forward. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
Year 2 restored him as Minister of the Court for Dependencies.
Year 2 restored him as Minister of Justice.
Same 都官尚書 office mistranslated as Dependencies. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
In the second year he was again Minister of the Court for Dependencies.
In the second year he was again Minister of Justice.
Same 都官尚書 office mistranslated as Dependencies. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
Jing reached Xinlin and drove Kan inside as deputy to the Prince of Xuancheng, commander of the city’s defense.
When Jing reached Xinlin, Kan was recalled into the city to serve as deputy to the Prince of Xuancheng, who commanded all military affairs within the walls.
追侃入 means urgently recalling Kan into the city, not Hou Jing driving/pursuing him in. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.
When Jing reached Xinlin, he pursued Kan into the city as deputy to the Prince of Xuancheng, commander of all forces within the walls.
When Jing reached Xinlin, Kan was recalled into the city to serve as deputy to the Prince of Xuancheng, who commanded all military affairs within the walls.
追 here is urgent summons/recall into defense duty, not Jing personally pursuing Kan. Independent source review refined the replacement for accuracy and natural English.

Earlier Kan’s eldest son Dan had been taken by Jing and brought beneath the wall to show Kan; Kan said to him: “I have poured out my clan for the lord and still regret it is not enough—how could I reckon on this one son? I hope you will kill him soon.”

Earlier Kan’s eldest son Dan had been taken by Jing and brought beneath the wall to show Kan; Kan said: “I have poured out my clan for the lord and still regret it is not enough—how could I reckon on this one son? I hope you will kill him soon.”
侃謂曰 with 殺之 addresses the captors about Dan; said to him wrongly makes Dan the addressee of kill him. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
Chengsheng year 3: Western Wei besieged Jiangling—Yun arrived too late and marched with Wang Senbian against Xiao Bo in the south.
In 554, Western Wei besieged Jiangling. Kun arrived too late to help and then accompanied Wang Sengyin against Xiao Bo in Lingnan.
The translation both misreads 鶤 as Yun and conflates 王僧愔 (Wang Sengyin) with the distinct 王僧辯 (Wang Sengbian), who appears in s0212. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.

When Hou Jing submitted, Yaren was told to lead Huan Hezhi of Shizhou, Zhan Haizhen of Renzhou, and thirty thousand picked men to Xuanchi to meet Jing—and to command seven provinces from Yu to Western Yu as Si-Yu inspector, based at Xuanchi.

When Hou Jing submitted, Yaren was told to lead Huan Hezhi of Shizhou, Zhan Haizhen of Renzhou, and thirty thousand picked men to Xuanhu to meet Jing—and to command seven provinces from Yu to Western Yu as Si-Yu inspector, based at Xuanhu.
懸瓠 is the place-name Xuanhu, not Xuanchi; the idiomatic English twice misrenders the toponym. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.

When Hou Jing surrendered, an edict ordered Yaren to supervise Huan Hezhi, Inspector of Shizhou, Zhan Haizhen, Inspector of Renzhou, and others with thirty thousand elite troops to hurry to Xuanchi to link with Jing; he also served as Area Commander of all military affairs for the seven provinces of Yu, Si, Huai, Ji, Yin, Ying, and Western Yu, and as Inspector of Si and Yu provinces, stationed at Xuanchi.

When Hou Jing surrendered, an edict ordered Yaren to supervise Huan Hezhi, Inspector of Shizhou, Zhan Haizhen, Inspector of Renzhou, and others with thirty thousand elite troops to hurry to Xuanhu to link with Jing; he also served as Area Commander of all military affairs for the seven provinces of Yu, Si, Huai, Ji, Yin, Ying, and Western Yu, and as Inspector of Si and Yu provinces, stationed at Xuanhu.
懸瓠 should be romanized Xuanhu; Xuanchi is a clear toponym error in the literal English. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
Taqing year 2: Jing broke faith; Yaren, Zhao Bochao, and Prince Huili of Nankang struck the rebels at the Eastern Directorate and were beaten in turn.
Taiqing year 2: Jing broke faith; Yaren, Zhao Bochao, and Prince Huili of Nankang struck the rebels at the Eastern Directorate and were beaten in turn.
太清 is standardly romanized Taiqing; Taqing is a corrupted reign-period spelling. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.

In the second year of Taqing, after Jing broke the alliance, Yaren joined Zhao Bochao and Prince Huili of Nankang to attack the rebels at the Eastern Directorate compound but was in turn defeated by the rebels.

In the second year of Taiqing, after Jing broke the alliance, Yaren joined Zhao Bochao and Prince Huili of Nankang to attack the rebels at the Eastern Directorate compound but was in turn defeated by the rebels.
太清 should be Taiqing in the literal English, matching the reign name. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.

If I end like this, I shall die with resentment still unspent.”
沒有餘憤 means lingering resentment would remain unspent in death; the idiomatic reverses this into having no wrath left. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
